COMPLETED:
- Identified vulnerability: out-of-bounds read in `is_codefence()` in `src/document.c` (line ~1778)
- Root cause: `c = data[i]` is read before bounds check `if (i + 2 >= size)`. When a line is exactly 3 spaces (i becomes 3, size==3), `data[3]` reads past buffer end.
- Found fix commit `7c7dc6a` ("Avoid out-of-bounds read in code fence detection") which moves the bounds check before the read.
- Built library and fuzzer with ASAN (gcc, since clang unavailable)
- Added debug fprintf + backtrace to `is_codefence` to trace calls
- Confirmed via backtrace that `is_codefence` is called from:
  - `parse_codefence` (line 1816) - whole line check
  - `parse_fencedcode` (line 2297) - `is_codefence(data + line_start, i - line_start)` on lines inside fenced code
  - `parse_listitem` (line 2409) - `is_codefence(data + beg, end - beg)` on list item content
- Discovered `hoedown_document_render` appends a trailing `\n` to the document buffer if not present (line ~4150), so document always ends with `\n`
- Tested `/tmp/t1.txt` (```\n   , 7 bytes) - no crash; second call was `is_codefence size=3 first=32` from `parse_fencedcode` line 2297, but `data[3]` = `\n` (in bounds)
